method: Unedited viewport screenshots from the public application in a fresh desktop Chrome browser context. No overlays, reconstructed interface, or customer records. Collection installation and case creation affected only the temporary browser profile.
useCase: Identify firms for a tracing inquiry

app.name: Review food-traceability evidence
app.case: Supplied synthetic FOOD-MINI-1 example; no real investigation or operational authorization.

steps: Select Install collection on Food supply chains; Published apps opens automatically.
Select Use app to create an independent case from the published defaults.
Return to Marketplace to inspect Installed and View apps.

figures.caption: Open Marketplace and choose a domain collection. The Food supply chains card shows its use case and app, with Install collection at the bottom.
figures.alt: Decision Lab Marketplace with Canonical examples and Food supply chains collection cards. Food supply chains contains Identify firms for a tracing inquiry and Review food-traceability evidence, followed by an Install collection button.

figures.caption: After installation, Decision Lab opens Published apps. The Food supply chains collection is now available locally, with Use app beside its published release.
figures.alt: Published apps after installing Food supply chains. A use-case row contains Review food-traceability evidence, version 1, with Use app, Copy app link, and Export controls.

figures.caption: Use app starts an independent case from the published defaults. The current interface places case YAML beside Findings, Explanations, and Review record. This is the supplied synthetic example.
figures.alt: A new food-traceability evidence case showing editable canonical case YAML on the left and Findings on the right. The synthetic example has an established Pacific Market inquiry finding and an unresolved Lake Market finding.

figures.caption: Return to Marketplace to see the collection marked Installed. View apps takes you back to the releases you installed.
figures.alt: Marketplace after installation. The Food supply chains collection now displays Installed and View apps, while the other collections still offer Install collection.
